item.chapter_label: Earth, Sun and the apparent motion of the sky
item.stem:
The diagram shows Earth with its rotation axis and the Pole Star. Ahana studies a long-exposure photo where most stars leave circular trails while the Pole Star stays nearly fixed.

Why does the Pole Star appear nearly stationary?

options.A: Earth's rotation axis points very close to the Pole Star.
options.B: Earth revolves around the Sun, and that revolution draws circular star trails around the Pole Star.
options.C: Other stars actually orbit the Pole Star.
options.D: Stars moving around the Pole Star make Earth rotate.
